title: Locus Of Control
description: Whether you believe outcomes are controlled by your own actions (internal locus) or by external forces like luck, fate, or powerful others (external locus).
shortDescription: Whether you believe outcomes are controlled by your own actions (internal locus) or by external forces like luck, fate, or powerful others (external locus).

sections.title: What It Is
sections.content: Whether you believe outcomes are controlled by your own actions (internal locus) or by external forces like luck, fate, or powerful others (external locus).

sections.title: Core Characteristics
content: Internal: “I make things happen.”
External: “Things happen to me.”

sections.title: Behavioral Patterns
content: Internals set goals, persist after failure, and seek information to improve.
Externals are more passive, may not attempt change, and attribute setbacks to outside forces.

sections.title: Communication Style
content: Internal: “I decided,” “I’ll fix it.”
External: “It’s out of my hands,” “What can you do?”

sections.title: Strengths
content: Internal: agency, motivation, resilience.
External: realistic acceptance of limits, less self‑blame for uncontrollable events.

sections.title: Weaknesses
content: Extreme internal: self‑blame for random misfortunes, burnout.
Extreme external: learned helplessness, lack of initiative.

sections.title: Decision-Making Style
content: Internals gather information, weigh options, feel responsible for outcomes.
Externals defer to luck, advice from others, or wait for circumstances to change.

sections.title: Relationship Patterns
content: Internals take responsibility for relationship problems, work to fix them.
Externals blame the partner or fate, may not try to improve.

sections.title: Workplace Behavior
content: Internals: proactive, seek feedback, advance faster.
Externals: wait for instructions, blame tools or management for poor performance.

sections.title: Leadership Style
content: Internal: decisive, accountable.
External: blame‑shifting, fatalistic.

sections.title: Stress Response
content: Internals feel control reduces stress—unless they can’t control the situation, then it increases.
Externals feel powerless, may give up earlier.

sections.title: How to Identify It
content: Ask: “When something goes wrong, what’s your first thought?”
Listen for language of responsibility vs. deflection.

sections.title: Common Misconceptions
content: Not a fixed trait; can shift with experience and environment.
An external locus isn’t always bad; sometimes things truly are out of our control.

sections.title: Real-World Scenario
sections.content: Two laid‑off workers. One updates her resume, networks, and finds a new job in a month. The other complains about the economy, blames his boss, and waits. Six months later, the first is employed, the second still waiting. Locus shaped outcome.

sections.title: Key Insight
sections.content: Whether you believe the pen is in your hand or the wind carries it, you’re right. The belief makes it true.
